# Who writes the brief down

Record 26 is a real brief from the real `seen-scout`, run against Sprint 0 ticket
SEEN-009 from this session, using the copy slice 1 generated. It cost the main
session one tool call and about thirty thousand tokens of a context that was not
this one, and it came back at 381 words against the cap of 400.

The provenance is worth stating once, because it is a property of the design
rather than an accident of this run: the scout holds no Write tool, so it cannot
put its brief on disk. It returns the brief to the session that asked, and the
session writes it to a file and records it. What is in the journal is therefore
the scout's content transcribed by the session: two HTML entities were turned back
into the angle brackets they came from, and a heading naming the question was
added. Nothing was added to the findings and nothing was cut.

That is the right trade. An agent that can write to disk is an agent that can
write to the journal, and a brief nobody read on the way in is a brief that could
carry anything into a record the ticket's evidence rests on. The alternative, a
scout with Write, would buy one fewer copy and paste at the price of the one thing
the read-only roster is for.

The consequence for anyone reading record 26 later: it is evidence that the scout
ran and what it found, not a byte-for-byte transcript of what the agent emitted.
